title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
summary: A jealous mother forces a young girl to hide with seven helpful little men.
coverScene: A young princess rests peacefully inside a glass bed while seven small men stand around her in a deep green forest.

sentences.text: Long ago, a very beautiful girl named Snow White lived in a big house.
She lived there with a woman who had a special glass that showed truth.
The special glass was able to speak to her every day.
It always gave a clear answer about who was the most beautiful person.
One day, the glass told the woman that Snow White was more beautiful.
Because of this, the woman wanted to send the girl away.
She asked a man to take Snow White deep into the forest.
However, the kind man could not kill Snow White at all.
He told her to run far away from the house.
The poor girl walked through the dark trees.
She found a small house owned by seven friendly little men.
The seven little men welcomed her inside the room.
They let her stay with them in their nice home.
Snow White helped them clean the rooms every day.
She also prepared food for them.
During this time, the woman learned from her special glass that Snow White was still breathing.
The woman decided to play a game with the girl.
She dressed up as an old person.
She went to the little house and gave Snow White a bad food item to eat.
As soon as Snow White bit the item, she fell down to the floor.
She seemed completely dead.
When the seven little men returned home that evening, they were very unhappy.
They found their good friend resting silent on the floor.
They built a special box for her because she looked so lovely.
The little men placed the box on a green land.
They could watch over her all the time.
Animals of the forest also came around to visit the sleeping girl.
After some time, a nice man traveled through the forest.
He saw the beautiful young girl inside the box.
He fell in love with her immediately.
He asked the little men if he could touch her face.
When the nice man moved her with care, the bad piece of food fell out from her open lips.
Snow White opened her eyes and stood up at last.
This made everyone very happy.

The dwarfs were in the forest.

sentences.text: Long ago, a very nice girl named Snow White lived in a big house with an angry woman.
The woman had a special device.
The device always told her the truth about who was the most beautiful person.
One day, the device told the woman that Snow White was much more lovely than herself.
Because of this, the bad woman wanted to get away from the young girl.
She asked a man to take her into the deep forest.
She wanted to be sure that the girl would never return to the house again.
The man agreed to help her because she was very powerful and dangerous.
They walked for many hours until they reached a very dark place.
Snow White felt afraid and did not know what would happen to her.
The man looked at her and felt sorry because she was so young and sweet.
He knew that he could not kill someone so pure.
He told her to run far away from the house.
The poor girl walked through the dark woods until she found a small building.
This building belonged to seven friendly men.
The seven men welcomed her inside and let her stay with them in their warm home.
Snow White helped them clean the rooms and cooked food for them every single day.
They enjoyed her company and gave her a clean bed to sleep in every night.
She felt happy and safe with her new friends in the deep forest.
The men went out to work every morning and told her to stay safe inside.
Snow White always locked the door and kept herself busy with house work.
She washed the dishes and cleared the floors until everything looked wonderful and clean.
The animals of the woods also came to visit her and brought her small gifts.
She sang songs with the birds and played games with the little dogs.
Meanwhile, the woman learned from her special device that Snow White was still alive.
She knew the girl was living in the forest.
The angry person decided to play with the girl herself.
She dressed up as an old person to fool the young child.
She went to the little house and gave Snow White bad food to eat.
As soon as Snow White bit the fruit, she fell down to the floor.
She seemed completely dead.
The bad woman smiled and walked away quickly back to her large house.
She thought that she had finally won and that no one would ever know the truth.
The device was quiet and did not say anything else about beauty that day.
The woman felt very proud of her bad plan and sat down to rest.
She hoped that the forest animals would take care of the body so she could forget everything.
When the seven men returned home that evening, they were extremely sad.
They found their dear friend down on the floor.
They built a special glass box for her.
She looked so lovely even in death.
The men placed the glass box on a green hill.
They could watch over her all the time from their small home.
Animals of the forest also came around to visit the sleeping girl and share their feeling.
The little birds sang sad songs every morning near the glass box.
The animals stayed close to the hill and protected her day and night.
None of the men could eat or sleep well because they missed her so much.
They kept fresh flowers around the box to show how much they loved their friend.
Weeks passed by and her face still looked as beautiful as the day she fell down.
After some time, a nice man traveled through the forest.
He saw the beautiful lady inside the glass box.
He fell in love with her immediately and asked the men if he could touch her face.
The friendly men allowed him to come close to the special box.
When the man moved her, the piece of bad food fell out from her mouth.
Snow White opened her eyes and woke up at last.
This made everyone wonderfully happy.
The men jumped and shouted with happiness because their dear friend was alive again.
The nice man smiled and asked her to travel with him to his wonderful home.
Snow White agreed and thanked the seven men for saving her life.
They all held each other and celebrated this amazing event together.
The bad woman never bothered them again, and they lived happily ever after.

sentences.text: Long ago, a very beautiful girl named Snow White lived in a grand castle.
She lived with a woman who felt bad about herself.
The woman possessed a magic mirror which always told the truth about who was the fairest person in the world.
One day, the magic mirror told the woman that Snow White was much more beautiful than herself.
Because of this, the angry woman wanted to get rid of the young girl.
She asked a hunter to take her into the deep forest.
She wanted him to make sure that the girl did not return to the castle ever again.
The woman gave him strict orders because she was so jealous of the child.
Every single morning, the queen would look into the glass and ask the same question.
The mirror would answer with the same truth, and the queen would become even more angry.
She could not stand the fact that someone else might be more lovely than her own reflection.
Therefore, the cruel queen made up her mind to destroy the innocent girl.
She believed that her life would be much better if Snow White was completely gone from the world.
The hunter had to obey the queen because she held all the power in the royal house.
He took the young girl away from the grand halls and led her deep into the green woods.
However, the kind hunter could not kill Snow White.
He looked at her sweet face and felt a lot of pity for her.
He told her to run away far from the castle.
The poor girl walked through the dark woods until she found a small house belonging to seven friendly small men.
The seven small men welcomed her inside.
They let her stay with them in their sweet home.
Snow White helped them clean the rooms every single day.
She cooked food for them as well.
The small men were very glad that she came to live with them in the forest.
They worked in the mountains during the day and returned home in the evening.
Snow White would prepare a warm meal and ensure the house was clean before they arrived back.
They shared many stories together and lived in peace for a long time.
The little men told her that she should never open the door to strangers while they were away.
Snow White promised that she would listen to their good advice.
She felt safe with her new friends in the cozy little cottage among the trees.
Meanwhile, the woman learned from her magic mirror that Snow White was still alive.
The mirror showed her that the girl was living in the forest with the seven small men.
The bad woman decided to trick the girl herself.
She dressed up as an old seller.
She went to the little house while the men were out working.
She gave Snow White a bad fruit to eat.
As soon as Snow White bit the fruit, she fell down to the floor.
She seemed completely dead after that moment.
The wicked queen smiled because she thought her plan had finally worked.
She left the little house quickly and returned to her grand castle before anyone could see her.
The forest became very quiet as the sun went down behind the high hills.
The birds stopped singing, and the wind blew softly through the leaves of the tall trees.
Everything was still in the woods while the poor girl lay motionless on the wooden floor.
The dark night covered the little house like a heavy blanket.
No one knew what had happened inside the small room during those quiet hours.
When the seven small men returned home that evening, they were extremely sad.
They found their dear friend down on the floor and not moving at all.
They cried and held her hands, but she did not wake up.
They built a special glass box for her.
She looked so lovely even in death.
The small men placed the glass box on a green hill.
They could watch over her all the time.
Animals of the forest also came around to visit the sleeping girl.
They came to share their sadness with each other.
The little birds sang quiet songs of grief near the glass box every morning.
The gentle deer stood by the hill and looked at Snow White with sad eyes.
No one wanted to leave the beautiful girl alone on the green grass.
The small men stayed close to the box day and night to protect her from any danger.
They hoped that some miracle might happen to bring their dear friend back to life.
Her skin remained as white as snow, and her lips stayed red like a rose.
After some time, a nice young man traveled through the forest.
He saw the beautiful young lady inside the glass box.
He fell in love with her immediately.
He asked the small men if he could touch her face.
When the young man moved her gently, the piece of bad fruit fell out from her mouth.
Snow White opened her eyes and woke up at last.
This made everyone wonderfully happy in the end.
The prince smiled down at her and thanked the small men for keeping her safe.
They celebrated together on the green hill where the glass box had rested for months.
The animals of the forest danced around them in pure joy.
Snow White got up and hugged her tiny friends with all her heart.
She climbed onto the horse with the handsome prince and waved goodbye to the little men.
They rode away toward the bright castle where a new life waited for them.
The wicked queen never bothered anyone ever again, and peace returned to the land.
Snow White and the prince lived happily together for the rest of their days.

sentences.text: Long ago, within the austere stone walls of a grand castle, lived a remarkably beautiful young girl whose name was Snow White.
She shared her opulent yet cold existence with a woman whose heart was consumed by bitterness and a fragile sense of self-worth.
At the center of the queen's troubled mind lay an ornate magic mirror, an artifact that never offered false comfort.
Every single morning, the vain queen would approach the glass and pose the very same question regarding who held the greatest beauty in the land.
So long as the mirror answered that she alone possessed the finest countenance, the queen remained content within her gilded cage.
One fateful morning, however, the silver surface rippled and delivered a verdict that shattered the queen's fragile world.
The mirror declared that Snow White, young and innocent, had surpassed the queen in grace and fairness.
A dark, corrosive jealousy took root within the royal chambers, poisoning the queen's thoughts day and night.
She could no longer bear the existence of someone whose mere reflection mocked her own fading youth.
Therefore, the cruel sovereign resolved to eliminate the girl, believing that only absolute erasure could restore her peace of mind.
Summoning a trusted hunter from the royal guard, the queen issued strict and merciless orders.
He was commanded to lead the young girl deep into the untamed forest and ensure she never returned to the castle.
Bound by the absolute power the queen held over the household, the troubled hunter had no choice but to obey.
He approached Snow White with feigned casualness, inviting her to walk with him beneath the ancient canopy of green trees.
The unsuspecting girl went along gladly, unaware of the grim purpose that had drawn them away from the safety of the halls.
Yet, as they penetrated deeper into the shadowy woods, the hunter found his resolve crumbling before the girl's gentle innocence.
He looked upon her sweet face and felt a profound wave of pity wash over his troubled conscience.
Dropping his gaze, he urged her to flee as far away from the castle as her feet could carry her.
The frightened girl turned and ran blindly through the thick undergrowth, driven by a sudden, desperate instinct for survival.
She traversed the dark and tangled woods for hours until the sprawling branches finally parted to reveal a modest, welcoming dwelling.
This secluded cottage belonged to seven industrious small men who mined the surrounding mountains for precious stones.
Upon returning from their daily labor, the friendly inhabitants discovered the exhausted girl resting near their threshold.
Moved by her plight, they welcomed her inside with open arms and offered their humble home as a safe sanctuary.
Snow White quickly adapted to her new life, finding profound comfort in the simple routines of domesticity.
Every day, she swept the wooden floors, dusted the corners, and prepared hearty meals for the tired workers.
The seven small men were immensely grateful for her warm presence, and the cottage soon echoed with laughter and shared stories.
Peace settled over the little woodland home, shielding them all from the bitter winds of the outside world.
Before leaving for the mountains each morning, however, the cautious men imparted a vital piece of advice.
They warned her never to open the heavy wooden door to any stranger while they were away laboring in the deep mines.
Snow White promised to heed their prudent words, feeling entirely secure within the embrace of her new friends.
Meanwhile, back in the grand castle, the queen's curiosity drove her once more to consult the polished surface of her magic glass.
To her fury, the mirror revealed that Snow White was not only alive but thriving deep within the forest.
Realizing the hunter had betrayed her, the wicked woman decided to take matters into her own hands.
She disguised herself as an elderly peddler, concealing her royal identity beneath a frayed cloak and a wrinkled mask.
Carrying a basket laden with deceptive goods, she journeyed through the winding forest paths until she reached the isolated cottage.
Finding the girl alone inside, the cunning visitor offered her a vibrant, sweet-smelling fruit with a deceptively alluring shine.
Snow White hesitated briefly, but the deceptive charm of the old woman lulled her lingering doubts into silence.
The moment the unsuspecting girl bit into the forbidden fruit, a dark numbness seized her limbs.
She collapsed instantly onto the wooden floor, her eyes closing as the spark of life seemingly left her frail body.
A triumphant smile crossed the wicked queen's face as she slipped away into the thickening shadows before anyone could return.
Evening descended upon the forest, wrapping the silent cottage in a heavy blanket of stillness and profound sorrow.
When the seven small men returned from the mountains, they found their beloved friend motionless upon the floor.
They wept bitterly, holding her cold hands and calling her name, but no breath of life answered their desperate pleas.
Unable to lower her into the dark earth, they constructed an exquisite box of clear glass to preserve her radiant beauty.
They carried the glass coffin to a verdant hillside, where they could watch over her vigilantly day and night.
The sorrow of her passing touched even the wild creatures of the forest, who gathered daily near the resting place.
Little birds sang mournful melodies each morning, while gentle deer stood nearby with soft, sorrowful eyes.
Her skin retained its snowy paleness, and her lips remained as vibrant as a red rose, defying the usual cruelties of death.
Months passed in this quiet vigil until a wandering young prince happened to ride through the shaded woods.
Catching sight of the breathtaking lady within the glass enclosure, he was instantly struck by a profound and overwhelming love.
He begged the mourning companions for permission to touch her face, marveling at the unnatural grace of her form.
As the young man gently shifted her position, the lodged piece of poisoned fruit slipped from her mouth.
Color rushed back to her cheeks as Snow White opened her eyes, drawing a deep breath after her long slumber.
Joy erupted on the green hill as the small men cheered and embraced their miraculously revived friend.
The prince thanked the loyal guardians, placed Snow White upon his majestic horse, and rode away toward a future of enduring peace.

options: The prince gently moved her, causing the poisoned fruit to fall from her mouth
